subject: Information Theory
title: Error Correction in Storage
description: A fast breakdown of Error Correction in Storage for builders.

hook.text: Your SSD silently corrects thousands of bit errors every second. You never notice because the codes work perfectly.

buildup.text: Flash memory degrades with each write cycle. After thousands of writes, cells become unreliable.

discovery.text: SSDs use BCH or LDPC codes internally. As cells age, the controller switches to stronger codes with more redundancy.

twist.text: Hard drives are similar: each sector has ECC bytes. Without them, drives would fail within hours of use.

climax.text: RAID systems add another layer: disk-level redundancy so an entire drive can fail without losing data.

punchline.text: Your data survives because layers of codes protect it.

quiz.question: Why do SSDs need increasingly strong error correction over time?
options: Flash memory cells degrade with each write cycle
